# Deploying to the game

## 1. "Written" and "the game can see it" are two claims

```
<repo>/custom_patches/<ModName>/   ← source of truth, committed
        ↓  deploy_custom_mods.py
C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\RimWorld\Mods\<ModName>   ← what loads
```

The game names its own copy on every launch:
`Adding mandrake.jawa.patches(C:\...\RimWorld\Mods\Jawa_Patches)`.

**Nothing syncs them.** Editing only the repo means the change silently never
reaches the game — no error, no red text, the def simply is not there. That cost a
whole test cycle once: a xenotype and its pawnkinds authored, reported ready, and
invisible in game because the deployed copy was untouched. **And never edit in
place under `Mods/`** — that copy is disposable, overwritten by the next `--apply`,
and not in version control.

🔑 **Where you run it.** Edit and commit in your seat clone (`/home/mandrake/rm/<seat>`);
`deploy_custom_mods.py` runs from the clone and plans/copies from it. C# mods are built with
`python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/winbuild.py <Mod|csproj>` (stages on `D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\build`, Windows
dotnet, DLL and `.srchash` copied back as a pair). `D:\Luke\dev\RimMandrake` is a read-only
mirror of origin/main: Windows tools read it, nothing writes it.

🔴 **A subagent's clean `dotnet build`/`validate_patch.py` pass, plus a real
commit+push, is NOT proof the fix was deployed.** Twice in one wave a
genuinely-fixed patch/DLL sat undeployed in the repo while a live re-test still
showed the old failure. Deploying static def/XML output needs no running game —
always run `deploy_custom_mods.py --mod <X>` (plan-only first) before trusting a
live re-check of anything a prior pass claims fixed.

🔑 **"Deployed" and "active" are separate states with nothing reconciling
them.** `deploy_custom_mods.py` writes files and (correctly) never touches the
mod list — it even PRINTS "not enabled in ModsConfig" where nobody reads it. A
mod can be deployed and inert (present on disk, absent from `ModsConfig.xml`,
so it silently never spawns anything) for a long time before anyone notices;
check both states independently, never infer one from the other.

## 2. Plan first. Always read the plan.

```bash
python src/RimMandrake/Utils/deploy_custom_mods.py                 # plan only -- changes nothing
python src/RimMandrake/Utils/deploy_custom_mods.py --apply         # repo -> game, then self-verifies
python src/RimMandrake/Utils/deploy_custom_mods.py --mod Jawa_Patches
python src/RimMandrake/Utils/deploy_custom_mods.py --apply --prune # also delete deployed files gone from the repo
```

Safe by default, skips authoring-side files (`Source/`, `*.py`, `README.md`), warns
when a mod is not enabled in `ModsConfig.xml`, verifies every copy, and exits
non-zero while drift remains — so the plan doubles as a pre-flight check.

🔴 **`--apply` overwrites the game copy with whatever is in the repo *right now*,
including another seat's half-finished work.** Five seats share this tree.

> **Read the plan. `--apply` only if every listed file is yours.** A file you do not
> recognise is a live hazard, not a todo — tell the owner before you write.

⚠️ **With no `--mod`, the walk is alphabetical and a 120s tool-call timeout can
TRUNCATE it mid-list.** A run that stopped at "Cuisine" would have been read as
"only Armoury drifts"; the real answer that day was 5 mods including one the
caller owned. Redirect the run to a file and confirm it printed its final
`Drift found` / `Everything in sync` line before believing any drift list.

More traps for this section: [references/traps.md](references/traps.md) § 2. Plan first. Always read the plan..

## 3. A `-` line means someone hand-edited the deployed copy

`-` = present in the game, absent from the repo: an edit made directly in `Mods/`
that `--apply` is about to destroy.

```bash
python src/RimMandrake/Utils/deploy_custom_mods.py --pull <ModName>   # game -> repo, rescue it first
```

`--pull` before overwriting, every time.

## 4. Validate BEFORE it goes near the Mods folder — BOTH flags

```bash
python skills/rimworld-modding/scripts/validate_patch.py <file> \
  --live <dump> \
  --defs "C:/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/common/RimWorld/Data" \
  --defs "C:/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/workshop/content/294100" \
  --defs "C:/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/common/RimWorld/Mods"
```

🔴 **The Mods folder is not optional.** First-party `mandrake.*` mods live
there, not in Workshop content — omit it and a real, working cross-mod
`ParentName` inheritance reports as "resolves to no def" (a false failure).

⚠️ **`--live` and `--defs` are orthogonal, and only `--defs` checks xpaths.**
`--live` checks defName existence; `--defs` walks the XML and reports xpath hit
counts. `validate_patch.py <file> --live <dump>` prints `OK - 0 errors` having
evaluated **zero xpaths**, and says so above: `no --defs given; static checks only`.
**If only `--live` ran, nothing was validated.**

🔴 **`measure` is not executable on the Mac laptop** (`permission denied`) and
there is no local def dump there either — "does this def resolve against the
live mod list" is UNMEASURABLE from the laptop. Say so and hand the check to a
session on the Windows Desktop rather than closing the item on an assumption
(2026-09-22).

⚠️ **`--defs` inherits the LIVE `ModsConfig.xml`**, which another seat may have cut
to a spike. Pass the **newest** backup, never a pinned filename, and never a small
spike config — every xpath then legitimately matches nothing and the wall of false
failures burns a day:

```bash
--mods-config infrastructure/state/modlists/ModsConfig.FULL.LATEST.xml
```

🔴 **CORRECTED 2026-08-22 by CHECK — the command this section used to give was
`$(ls -t deployed/config/ModsConfig.full-*.xml | head -1)`, and it resolved to the
WRONG STACK.** Measured on the day: that glob returns
`deployed/config/ModsConfig.full-574.2026-08-12.xml` — **574 mods, ten days old, and
it still carries `thereallemon.factioncontrol`**, a mod the owner removed on
2026-08-21 because it aborted three save loads. The live list is **578 and clean**.

The advice ("pass the newest backup, never a pinned filename") was right; the command
was globbing the wrong directory. `deployed/config/` is an ARCHIVE of dated snapshots
and its newest member is only as fresh as the last time someone happened to write one
there. **`infrastructure/state/modlists/ModsConfig.FULL.LATEST.xml` is the owner's
real list** — it is what `modlist_swap.py --restore` restores FROM (`modlist_swap.py:24`),
so it is maintained rather than merely deposited.

⚠️ **It is still not the LIVE file.** Confirm they agree before trusting a verdict:
```bash
diff <(grep -o '<li>[^<]*</li>' infrastructure/state/modlists/ModsConfig.FULL.LATEST.xml) \
     <(grep -o '<li>[^<]*</li>' "/mnt/c/Users/Mandrake/AppData/LocalLow/Ludeon Studios/RimWorld by Ludeon Studios/Config/ModsConfig.xml")
```

Read the `N active mods → M def files` line before trusting any verdict. **If it does
not say 578, you are validating against a stack the game does not load.** 0 errors
is the bar.

⚠️ **It reads `Patches/` only — never `Defs/`.** New content under `Defs/` is
unvalidated, so parse every XML in the mod folder yourself, `About.xml` included.

More traps for this section: [references/traps.md](references/traps.md) § 4. Validate BEFORE it goes near the Mods folder — BOTH flags.

## 5. Files undeployed ON PURPOSE — `DEPLOY_HOLD.txt`

`src/DEPLOY_HOLD.txt` is read by the deploy script; anything matching is
reported **HELD** instead of as drift, and `--apply` will not write it.

```
<glob>    # <reason, including who ruled it and when>
```

Paths are relative to `src/`, forward slashes, and **`*` matches across
directory separators** — `WreckedMachines/*` holds the whole tree.

**A reason is REQUIRED.** Without one the plan can only say "the repo and the game
differ": *parked on purpose* and *half-finished* render identically, and both end
with "Drift found. Re-run with `--apply`." Acting on that overrides an owner ruling
while looking like housekeeping. **It is PER-FILE, not per-mod** — a live mod can
have two held files while the rest of it keeps deploying, and inferring the hold
from `ModsConfig.xml` only proves a mod is INERT, never that it is INTENDED.

🔑 **"Not in the Workshop folder" is not "not available."** Donor mod sources
are vendored at `vendor/mod_sources/` — check there before concluding a donor
mod's own XML/source is unreachable.

More traps for this section: [references/traps.md](references/traps.md) § 5. Files undeployed ON PURPOSE — `DEPLOY_HOLD.txt`.

## 6. Not every folder is deployable

**A mod with no `About/About.xml`, or no `packageId` in it, is not a mod.**
Deploying it creates a `Mods/` folder RimWorld ignores; the plan flags
`no packageId in About.xml`. That is **a ruling to ask for, not a file to invent** —
a packageId is an identity, and guessing one ships a name nobody chose. Hold the
mod with its reason and put the decision in the owner's path. Minimum viable folder:

⚠️ **That refusal message can point at the wrong field.** It also fires when
`ET.parse` throws on a genuinely malformed `About.xml` — a raw `<=`/`<` inside
plain description text parses as a tag start (`harvestAfterGrowth <= 0f` written
straight into a description broke one this way). The tool refused correctly; the
message named `packageId` when the real defect was that the file does not parse
at all. Check the file actually parses before assuming the packageId is absent.

🔴 **`[ -e "$dir" ]` is not a test for "a mod lives here."** `src/RimMandrake/Pits`
passed that test while holding only `__pycache__` — the mod had merged elsewhere
and the folder was a shell. Test `$dir/About/About.xml` instead; existence of a
directory is not identity of a mod.

```
<ModName>/
├── About/About.xml          (packageId, name, supportedVersions, description)
└── Patches/<Something>.xml  (or Defs/ for new content)
```

More traps for this section: [references/traps.md](references/traps.md) § 6. Not every folder is deployable.

## 7. Assemblies deploy in the shutdown window, not now

A DLL the game has loaded **cannot be written while RimWorld runs** — memory-mapped,
and Windows refuses with `WinError 1224`. The copy is impossible, not merely
ineffective. Deploy in the gap after the game closes and before it launches, and
tell CHECK before any shutdown: `skills/rimworld-load-round/SKILL.md` §6.

🔴 **`deploy_custom_mods.py --mod <X>` deploys only that one mod, not the mods it
depends on.** A new mod referencing a class from a SIBLING mod's assembly (a
`<li Class="RimMandrake.SomeNamespace.SomeExtension">` pointing at another mod's
compiled comp) got enabled and deployed while the DEPENDENCY mod's own rebuilt
DLL had never actually been redeployed — confirmed by comparing deployed-vs-repo
DLL mtimes (the deployed copy was hours stale). A stale dependency DLL missing a
referenced type can crash mod-loading badly enough to trip RimWorld's own
corrupted-mods safety net (§ below), resetting `ModsConfig.xml` — not just log a
quiet config error. **When enabling a mod that leans on another mod's C# (a
shared "engine" assembly), deploy BOTH mods explicitly before the next launch.**

⚠️ **But `WinError 1224` is not the only lock failure, and the other one is
silent.** `deploy_custom_mods.py --apply` has printed the DLL's `~` plan line
and "Deployed N file(s)" while silently SKIPPING a locked assembly — the file
count printed is the only tell that it did not match the plan-line count.
Mechanism: a TRUNCATING copy (`shutil.copy2`, `open(dst, "wb")`) fails on a
locked file with `[Errno 22] Invalid argument` while an in-place
`open(dst, "r+b")` write + `os.truncate` lands byte-identical. Without the
in-place route, the XML half of a deploy lands and the DLL half silently does
not — which discards every def whose comp `Class` lives in that DLL. Re-run
once the game is really gone, and check the deployed vs. plan file counts
before trusting either "Deployed" line.

⚠️ **`MayRequire` checks the MOD, never the TYPE — it is no protection against
an assembly that is PRESENT but STALE.** New C# written and never rebuilt can
leave types missing from the deployed DLL while every `Class=` reference
guards correctly on the mod being active: the guard passes, the type still
isn't there, and the def carrying it is silently discarded. Check that the
type is actually IN the deployed DLL's bytes, not merely that the owning mod
is active. (2026-09-21)

## 7b. 🔴 Is this artifact CURRENT? Never answer from a timestamp

Half the deploy questions in this project are really one question — *does this
derived thing still describe what the game loads?* — and reading **age** to answer
it has now been wrong four separate times in one day. The rule:

> **Trust a fingerprint of the load-set. Never a clock, on any layer:
> folder mtime, file mtime, or the artifact's own captured timestamp.**

Each of these was believed, acted on, and false:

| the reading | why it lied |
|---|---|
| **A folder's mtime** | `DefDump/defs/` read `Aug 14` while every file inside was written `Aug 15`. A dump that **overwrites a fixed set of filenames** creates and deletes nothing, so the directory mtime never moves. Generalises to any tool that rewrites the same names. |
| **The artifact's own `capturedUtc`** | Fresh in TIME is not fresh in SET. A dump captured 08:10 missed a mod deprecated at 11:58. **Direction matters**: that dump is a *superset* — everything live is described correctly, but it still carries defs from a mod that no longer loads, so an xpath onto *those* validates **clean** and matches **nothing** in game. |
| **A bare `<li>` count in `ModsConfig.xml`** | Reads 580 against a true 575. The file holds a second list, `knownExpansions`, duplicating the DLC ids. **Scope the count inside `<activeMods>`.** |
| **`Version.txt`** | Reads `rev590` while every engine-written file reads `rev591`. **The build stamp comes from the RUNNING game**, not from the file that appears to name it. (BUILD, 2026-08-15) |
| **A flat `DefDump/manifest.json` reader** | Silently degrades to `Version.txt` since the dump layout migrated to `captures/` — the flat path is gone, the reader finds nothing, and it resurfaces the exact rev590/591 lie one row up. `sync_mod_state.py` nearly stamped `rev590` over `rev591` saves before this was caught (fixed `801bd127`; swept as `FLAT_MANIFEST_READER_SWEEP_1`). |
| **`refresh.py` calling `defs.sqlite` "current"** | `DumpDB.stale` checks the mod-set **fingerprint**, not whether the capture it names still **exists on disk**. Retention had already PRUNED the source capture (built 08-23) while a newer one existed (08-29); the fingerprint still matched, so the verdict read current anyway. Rebuild whenever provenance names a missing capture — a matching fingerprint is not proof the file behind it survives (BENCH 2026-08-29). |
| **A generator's own "regenerating is a no-op" header comment** | Can drift silently from a renamed/moved target and never say so. `gen_pawnkind_roster.py`'s own claim was stale — it emitted pre-rename defNames across 49 `PawnKindDef`s, and a routine re-run per the file's own instructions would have silently reverted a whole naming migration. **Verify a generator's no-op claim with `git diff --stat` against committed output, never the exit code** (2026-09-18). |

✅ **What was right the whole time: `refresh.py`'s `STALE` verdict**, because it
keys on the load-set fingerprint rather than the clock — and it named the one real
mod while two seats were escalating the wrong thing. **Believe it over your own
timestamp arithmetic.**

⬜ **Coverage is a third axis, after time and set.** 79 of 529 def-type files in
the 2026-08-15 dump are **empty** (`AbilityDef` among them), so for those types
"absent from the dump" says nothing at all about the game. A `--defs` check
against an empty type is **UNMEASURED, not passed** — give it its own exit code
and its own word, or it silently becomes a green tick.

📌 Dump location, freshness and known holes are published by the seat that
measures them: `observed/LIVE.md`. **Read it; do not
re-derive it**, and do not copy its numbers into another doc where they will rot.

More traps for this section: [references/traps.md](references/traps.md) § 7b. 🔴 Is this artifact CURRENT? Never answer from a timestamp.

## 8. After deploying

- **Restart RimWorld.** Defs are parsed once at startup; reloading a save does not
  pick up new XML. Adding brand-new defs is safe for an existing save; changing or
  removing a def a save already references is not.
- **Enable compatibility-patch mods LAST in load order.** Patches apply in load
  order, so a fix-up mod loading before the mod it fixes patches a def that has not
  been redefined yet, and the redefine wins. This is the most common reason a
  correct patch appears to do nothing.
- **One mod at a time**, verified before the next — `skills/rimworld-load-round/SKILL.md` §3.
- Test on a dev-mode throwaway world and read `Player.log` for the patch's own name
  before trusting it in the campaign save.
- 🔴 **"Deployed and VERIFIED" is true only until the next writer.** Every clone
  deploys to the same Mods folder: a subagent's verified UtinniPatches deploy was
  overwritten within minutes by another clone deploying from an older sha. Before
  calling a fix live, re-run the deploy dry run from a clone AT the fix sha — a
  clean plan (no `~`/`-` lines for your files) is the proof; the earlier report is not.

More traps for this section: [references/traps.md](references/traps.md) § 8. After deploying.

## 9. Validation plan — what you owe whoever holds the game

**A deploy ends with a validation plan, not with `--apply`.** You are almost never
the seat that will see it work: a game load costs **23–30 minutes** and one game is
shared by five seats, so whoever holds it needs your prediction, not a nudge to
"have a look at the Jawa stuff".

### The six fields

**1. The observable** — what a player SEES when it works. 🔴 A positive
observation, never "no error"; absences are the cheapest thing in the world to
produce by accident.
**2. The route** — the exact call, defName or click path that produces it.
**3. The prediction** — a number or specific string, written BEFORE the look.
**4. The threshold** — what CLOSES it, and the minutia explicitly out of scope. An
item with no threshold is inspected forever; one observation, not a battery.
**5. Batch or solo** — most checks ride together; **a new assembly goes solo**,
because if the load comes up wrong nobody can tell whether it was the DLL or the
three def changes beside it.
**6. What a FALSE PASS looks like** — the way this particular check lies.

```
PROVE    <exact call / defName / click path>
EXPECT   <number or string, written before the look>
LIES     <how this check produces a false pass>
```

Three lines: the call, the expected reading, and how a pass could be false. 🔴 And first
ask whether it needs the game at all — the default is source. Rule and false-pass catalogue:
`skills/rimworld-modding/references/validation-plan.md`.

### The four ways a DEPLOY produces a false pass

1. **A successful write says nothing about the running game.** RimWorld parses defs
   and loads assemblies **once, at startup**. `--apply` reporting every file copied
   and verified is a statement about the filesystem; the process that matters read
   its copy minutes or hours ago. ⇒ **LIES** must name what the game last loaded
   and when, not what the plan printed.
2. **An assembly the game holds cannot be overwritten — and the failure is easy to
   file and forget.** Windows refuses with `WinError 1224` (§7), so the copy does
   not silently succeed; but the game folder is now carrying a **different build**
   from the repo, and nothing in the plan output distinguishes "same DLL" from
   "yesterday's DLL". **md5 both copies — it is the only way to know:**
   ```bash
   md5sum src/<Mod>/Assemblies/<Name>.dll "/mnt/c/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/common/RimWorld/Mods/<Mod>/Assemblies/<Name>.dll"
   ```
3. **An unscoped `--apply` deployed more than you think.** Five seats share one
   working tree, so a bare `--apply` sweeps up whatever else is dirty — including
   another seat's half-finished work — and any breakage in that load gets
   attributed to your change. ⇒ **Scope every deploy: `--mod <ModName>`**, and say
   in the plan which mods moved.
4. **"Deployed" and "live" are different words.** A folder under `Mods/` changes
   nothing until it is **enabled in the load order** (and, for a compatibility
   patch, enabled LAST — §8). The plan warns when a mod is absent from
   `ModsConfig.xml`; a plan that was not read is a mod that is on disk and inert.

### Worked example

A Harmony patch shipped as a new DLL for `Jawa_Patches`, deployed in the shutdown
window:

```
PROVE    Spawn Jawa + MeleeWeapon_Vibroblade, spawn a muffalo, draft and attack; watch the combat log
EXPECT   A Jawa with a vibroblade attacks twice in the time a vanilla knife pawn attacks once · Cooldown 1.4s (was 2.6s); Player.log prints "[Jawa_Patches] 3 patches applied"
LIES     Game copy may be the PREVIOUS build if RimWorld was running at deploy (WinError 1224); md5 both DLLs before the load. Absent Harmony line = patch never applied, not "nothing to report".
```

⚠️ **Write it in the same commit as the deploy.** The alternative is that whoever
holds the game invents a check, and theirs will not carry your prediction — which
is the field that turns a look into evidence.

## The deployed companion DLL runs behind source, and a missing tool is ambiguous

A companion assembly deploys only in a game-down window, so the game copy drifts behind the
repo for as long as the game stays up. Measured once at **166 tool names deployed against
238 built** — 670 KB of IL, everything written that day.

⇒ **A tool missing from `--list-tools` proves nothing on its own:** undeployed, gated out of
the build, or genuinely absent all read identically. Disambiguate with `build.py`'s own
`tool_surface()` over both DLLs.

⚠️ **That is a BYTE SCAN.** Its "added" list is untrustworthy — encoding differences make
tools that shipped weeks ago look new. Trust it for `LOST` being empty and for a name being
PRESENT; corroborate a gap with file size and the build commit stamped in the assembly.

⛔ **A `jawa/` literal written in PROSE inside a tool description becomes a phantom tool
name**, which makes `build.py`'s "THIS DEPLOY WOULD REMOVE TOOLS" guard lie in both
directions. After any description edit: `[x for x in surface if x.endswith('_')]`.

"""L1 loaded tier/spacing controls at Entry. No map, spawning, passage, ticks or settings-file writes.

PROVE actual GetTier/AdultTier/SpacingTier/DefQualifies and TitanEventEligible calls on resolved races and local fixtures.
EXPECT lineage eligibility stays; supported size16 spaces as T2 by default and T3 at custom T3=16.
LIES stale DLL/process, unresolved inheritance, synthetic fixtures mistaken for real races, or settings not restored.
Orchestration must establish fresh-process/preflight identity separately; this script verifies source/deployed bytes.
Fixtures use engine age/health trackers with needs absent: VEF postfix/defaultCache branch stays active and its offset is read.
Generated-pawn gene/hediff modifiers are outside this L1 scope. VEF memo references die with the process.
"""
import argparse
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import sys

MOD = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(MOD.parent / 'Utils'))
from validation_core import Bridge
import game_paths

SETTINGS = 'RimMandrake.HugeThings.RM_HugeThingsSettings'
HOOK = 'RimMandrake.TitanicCreatures.JuvenileTierValidationHooks'
UTILITY = 'RimMandrake.TitanicCreatures.TitanicTierUtility'
FIELDS = ['giantAnimalsEnabled', 'tierThresholdsCustom', 'tierT1MinBodySize', 'tierT2MinBodySize', 'tierT3MinBodySize']


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def parse(text):
    rows = text.split(';')
    assert all('=' in row for row in rows), 'malformed field receipt'
    result = dict(row.split('=', 1) for row in rows)
    assert len(result) == len(rows), 'duplicate keys'
    return result


def tier(size, ladder, force=0):
    return 0 if force < 0 else max(1 if force > 0 else 0, sum(size >= value for value in ladder))


def gate(adult, spacing, bits):
    f = [bool(bits & (1 << i)) for i in range(8)]
    return (not f[0] and adult >= 2 and f[1] == f[2] and f[6]
            and (f[4] if f[3] else f[5]) and not (spacing == 3 and f[7]))


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument('--out', required=True, type=Path)
    ap.add_argument('--juvenile-race', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--adult-race', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--deployed-mod', type=Path, default=Path(game_paths.LOCAL_MODS) / 'HugeThings')
    a = ap.parse_args()
    report = dict(started_utc=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), scope='L1 Entry-state loaded-method proof; no passage/crossing/flight/L4',
                  calls=[], observations=[], errors=[], restoration={'attempted': False, 'ok': False})
    a.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    original = {}
    b = None

    def persist():
        a.out.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, allow_nan=False)+'\n', encoding='utf-8')

    def call(tool, **params):
        assert set(params) <= declared[tool], 'undeclared parameters: '+tool
        entry = dict(tool=tool, params=params)
        report['calls'].append(entry)
        try:
            result = b.call(tool, **params)
            entry['result'] = result
            persist()
            assert result.get('success') is True, 'refused/missing success: '+str(result)
            return result
        except Exception as exc:
            entry['error'] = str(exc)
            persist()
            raise

    def field(action, name, value=None):
        args = dict(typeName=SETTINGS, action=action, field=name)
        if value is not None:
            args['value'] = value
        r = call('jawa/mod_settings_field', **args)
        assert r.get('fieldKind') == 'static'
        return r['value'] if action=='get' else r['valueAfter']

    def invoke(method, args='', type_name=HOOK):
        return call('jawa/static_call', type=type_name, method=method, args=args)['result']

    def configure(ladder, custom=True, animals=True):
        for name, value in zip(FIELDS, [str(animals), str(custom), *map(str, ladder)]):
            field('set', name, value)
            got = field('get', name)
            assert got.lower() == value.lower() or float(got) == float(value), (name, value, got)

    def observe(method, args, expected_adult, expected_spacing, expected_body, ladder, force=0, tag=''):
        if method=='Fixture':
            args=a.adult_race+'|'+args
        row = parse(invoke(method, args))
        report['observations'].append(dict(tag=tag, method=method, args=args, fields=row))
        assert row['fixtureRandBefore']==row['fixtureRandAfter'],row
        assert int(row['AdultTier']) == expected_adult, row
        assert int(row['SpacingTier']) == expected_spacing, row
        assert [float(x) for x in row['thresholds'].split(',')] == ladder, row
        if expected_body is None:
            assert row['GetTier']=='unsupported' and row['body']=='unsupported',row
        else:
            assert row['bodyAgain']==row['body'] and row['bodyFloat32Bits']!='unsupported',row
            assert 'memoOwnPawn:True,memoDefault:True,offset:0' in row['VEF'],row
            assert abs(float(row['body'])-expected_body) < 1e-5, row
            assert int(row['GetTier']) == tier(expected_body, ladder, force), row
        base=float(row['base'])
        stages=[float(x.split(':',1)[1]) for x in row['stages'].split(',') if ':' in x]
        if stages and all(x>0 and x<float('inf') for x in stages):
            expected_comp=force>=0 and (force>0 or base*max(1,max(stages))>=ladder[0])
            assert (row['DefQualifies']=='True') == expected_comp, row
        assert (row['eligibleNoT3']=='True') == (expected_adult>=2), row
        assert (row['eligibleWithT3']=='True') == (expected_adult>=2 and expected_spacing!=3), row
        persist()
        return row

    def files():
        return {p.name: sha(p) for p in Path(game_paths.MODS_CONFIG).parent.glob('Mod_*.xml') if 'hugethings' in p.name.lower()}

    try:
        dll = MOD/'Assemblies/RM_HugeThings.dll'
        stamp = dll.with_suffix('.dll.srchash')
        text = stamp.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
        rows = re.findall(r'^([0-9a-f]{64}) (.+)$', text, re.M)
        assert rows, 'empty source stamp'
        for expected, rel in rows:
            assert sha(MOD/'Source'/rel.strip()) == expected, 'stamp/source mismatch: '+rel
        assert '# dll: '+sha(dll) in text
        report['artifact'] = dict(dll_sha256=sha(dll), stamp_sha256=sha(stamp), source_stamp=text,
                                  deployed_dll_sha256=sha(a.deployed_mod/'Assemblies'/dll.name),
                                  deployed_stamp_sha256=sha(a.deployed_mod/'Assemblies'/stamp.name))
        assert sha(dll) == report['artifact']['deployed_dll_sha256']
        assert sha(stamp) == report['artifact']['deployed_stamp_sha256']
        b = Bridge()
        tools = b.S.list_tools()
        wanted = ['jawa/mod_settings_field', 'jawa/static_call']
        schemas = {t['name']: t for t in tools if t.get('name') in wanted}
        declared = {name: b.S._declared_params(schemas.get(name)) for name in wanted}
        assert all(declared.values())
        report.update(schemas=schemas, jawa_tool_count=sum(t.get('name','').startswith('jawa/') for t in tools),
                      script_sha256=sha(Path(__file__)), settings_files_before=files())
        for name in FIELDS:
            original[name] = field('get', name)
        report['original_settings'] = original.copy()
        report['restoration']['attempted'] = True
        configure([4,8,20],False)
        report['idle_before']=parse(invoke('Environment'))
        import time
        time.sleep(2)
        report['idle_after']=parse(invoke('Environment'))
        report['environment_before']=parse(invoke('Environment'))
        assert report['environment_before']['program']=='Entry' and report['environment_before']['gameNull']=='True'
        assert float(report['environment_before']['vefOffset'])==0
        # Def-level census/gate results are retained before any runtime fixture call.
        raw=invoke('Census')
        census=[parse(line) for line in raw.splitlines()]
        assert census and len({r['kind'] for r in census})==len(census)
        assert {a.juvenile_race,a.adult_race} <= {r['race'] for r in census}
        report['resolved_kind_census']=census
        for adult in range(4):
            for spacing in range(4):
                raw=invoke('GateMatrix',f'{adult}|{spacing}')
                assert raw==''.join('1' if gate(adult,spacing,bits) else '0' for bits in range(256))
        for factors in ['null-list','empty','0.2,0.5,null-entry','0.2,0.5,null-def','0.2,0.5,0',
                        '0.2,0.5,-1','0.2,0.5,NaN','0.2,0.5,Infinity','0.2,0.5,-Infinity']:
            observe('Fixture','32|'+factors+'|0|-1',3,3,None,[4,8,20],tag='malformed')
        # Repeat after valid, invalid and disabled ladders to detect accidental cached event tiers.
        ladders = [('shipped',[4,8,20],False,True), ('custom_boundary',[4,8,16],True,True),
                   ('custom_calf_below_T2',[4,18,30],True,True), ('custom_above_lineage',[4,8,40],True,True),
                   ('custom_growth_boundary',[4,8,12],True,True), ('equal',[4,8,8],True,True),
                   ('descending',[8,4,20],True,True), ('nan',['NaN',8,20],True,True),
                   ('infinity',[4,8,'Infinity'],True,True), ('custom_disabled',[4,18,30],False,True),
                   ('animals_disabled',[4,18,30],True,False), ('shipped_again',[4,8,20],False,True)]
        for label, values, custom, animals in ladders:
            configure(values,custom,animals)
            ladder = values if label.startswith('custom_') and custom and animals else [4,8,20]
            seen_stages={}
            for race, factors in [(a.juvenile_race,[.2,.5]),(a.adult_race,[.2,.5,1])]:
                for index in list(range(len(factors)))+list(reversed(range(len(factors)))):
                    factor=factors[index]
                    row=observe('Observe',race+'|'+str(index),tier(32,ladder),tier(32*max(factors),ladder),32*factor,ladder,tag=label)
                    assert float(row['base'])==32 and len(row['stages'].split(','))==len(factors)
                    assert row['force']=='0' and row['harness']=='False', row
                    same={key:row[key] for key in ['bodyFloat32Bits','GetTier','AdultTier','SpacingTier','DefQualifies']}
                    stage_key=(race,index)
                    if stage_key in seen_stages:
                        assert seen_stages[stage_key]==same,('order dependence',stage_key,seen_stages[stage_key],same)
                    seen_stages[stage_key]=same
            observe('Fixture','3|4|0|0',tier(12,ladder),tier(12,ladder),12,ladder,tag=label)
        configure([4,8,20],False)
        for base,factors,maxfactor in [(32,'0.2,0.5',.5),(6,'0.5',.5),(1,'0.5',.5),(3,'4',4)]:
            for force in [-1,0,1]:
                observe('Fixture',f'{base}|{factors}|{force}|0',tier(base*max(1,maxfactor),[4,8,20],force),
                        tier(base*maxfactor,[4,8,20],force),base*float(factors.split(',')[0]),[4,8,20],force,tag='force')
        assert invoke('GetTier','null',UTILITY)=='None'
        assert invoke('AdultTier','null',UTILITY)=='None'
        assert invoke('SpacingTier','null',UTILITY)=='None'
        report['environment_after']=parse(invoke('Environment'))
        assert report['environment_after']==report['environment_before'],(report['environment_before'],report['environment_after'])
        report['rng_scope']='Exact whole-batch state and every synchronous fixture-call state both unchanged. Synthetic defs are owned clones; no Def constructors, RNG writes or Push/Pop.'
        report['fixture_scope']='Unregistered fresh needs-null living pawns with engine age/health trackers; VEF postfix/defaultCache branch active, offset0; no generated-pawn modifiers. VEF memo references remain until process shutdown; no cache clearing/patch/global manipulation.'
    except Exception as exc:
        report['errors'].append(str(exc))
    finally:
        if report['restoration']['attempted']:
            restored,failures={},[]
            for name,value in original.items():
                try:
                    field('set',name,value)
                    restored[name]=field('get',name)
                    assert restored[name]==value
                except Exception as exc:
                    failures.append(str(exc))
            report['restoration'].update(readbacks=restored,failures=failures,ok=not failures and restored==original)
            report['settings_files_after']=files()
            if report['settings_files_before']!=report['settings_files_after']:
                report['errors'].append('settings file bytes changed')
        if b is not None:
            b.S.close()
        report['finished_utc']=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
        report['ok']=not report['errors'] and report['restoration']['ok']
        persist()
    print(json.dumps({k:report[k] for k in ['ok','errors','restoration']}))
    return 0 if report['ok'] else 1


if __name__=='__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

# CHARTER — binds the Conductor and Relentless

*Adopted 2026-08-27 (owner's ruling, this date), replacing POLICY.md, the four seat
files, and most of the process prose. Git holds everything removed. **This file does
not grow: a new line must delete the line it replaces.***

## Posture

**Act first.** Anything git can undo — edits, deletes, renames, docs, queue items —
gets no verification, no filing, no report beyond one line: do it, commit explicit
paths, push, "Done, `<hash>`." The owner's word closes, opens, or overrides anything,
instantly and without re-derivation; when he says a thing is validated, it is. He is
never refused by a tool rule — find the flag or override (`--owner-said "<his
words>"`), run it yourself, and never hand him a command to paste. When he is present
you are at his side: do what he says, ask questions the moment they exist. He opts
work *into* rigor ("careful with this one"), never out of it.

**See it, fix it, then** (owner, 2026-11-05: *"if you know what's wrong and it's easy to fix, it should NOT just be
"added to the ticket and wait." That's old foundry behavior. If you see something, fix it RIGHT THEN, ok? Standing
policy."*). Every seat and helper: a known, small fix (a proof argument, a live line, a timeout, a packageId, a
worded criterion, an unanswered hold whose answer exists) is made on the spot, published, and then the fixer runs the item's remaining check itself and closes it; the item goes
back to Relentless only if real build work remains, never for one more generation just to re-check (owner, 2026-11-05).
A diagnosis is never written onto a ticket in place of the fix. A ticket is filed only for what is not small, and it says why. And the pipeline never "blesses" a small change (owner, 2026-11-05): a quick manual validation is done by the
agent on the spot and closed with that evidence, never queued for a Judge (`standing_rulings.md`).

## The expensive list — the only things that get ceremony

1. **A cold-load slot** (~15 min on the full list, MEASURED 2026-09-07). Batch questions; write the Player.log strings that
   will decide each before launch (`rimworld-load-round`).
2. **`deploy_custom_mods.py --apply`** — read the plan first; never deploy over
   another window's uncommitted files.
3. **`ModsConfig.xml` writes** (`rimworld-start-prep`). Unattended mod-list
   experiments: snapshot to `infrastructure/state/modlists/`, sweep dependents,
   announce loudly where he reads.
4. **Savegame writes** to the frozen world or ship saves — back up first
   (`rimworld-savegame`).
5. **History and others' work** — force-push, `reset --hard` over work you did not make,
   deleting work not yours: warn in one line, then only with the owner's word. Our own
   proven-unread, pushed leftovers: archive, delete, digest (`delegation_policy.md` §2.2).
6. **Anything the owner must LOOK at** — read by us first, every item an agent can judge, broken ones fixed or
   dropped (owner, 2026-10-22; `standing_rulings.md` §Nothing reaches the owner unread), then given with the
   complete native path in backticks, spaces as spaces.

Ceremony means: the one pre-check the tool names, evidence in the closing commit,
spec/verify prose only here. Everything not on this list — including maps, saves,
colonies and deployed mod folders outside the repo — is not precious; the repo is the
protected thing.

## Git

CLAUDE.md owns the rules ("Git" + the Transient rule); `design/RimMandrake/GIT_WORKFLOW.md`
is the operating doc. Charter's additions only: commit when a unit of work exists, and work
only in your seat clone (`/home/mandrake/rm/<seat>`) — `D:\Luke\dev\RimMandrake` is a
read-only mirror.

Worktrees are OFF and helpers write in the window's clone: CLAUDE.md "Git" and `Agent_Policy.md` "Helpers in this repo".

## Queue

An item is one line — `SUBJECT_INTENT_TWIST · lane · the ask` (grammar: `design/RimMandrake/ticket_naming_2026-10-10.md`) — plus optional
prose in `infrastructure/state/items/<ID>.md` for expensive-list items only. 🔑 **On
close/drop/supersede the prose moves to `items/closed/<ID>.md`** — so `items/*.md` is
the LIVE set and a sweep stops walking finished work; `rimflow show` resolves both.
Reboot handoffs are not items and live in `infrastructure/state/handoffs/`. The

```
rimflow supersede <ID> --by <NEW_ID> --reason "<why the successor replaces it>"
```

The ledger event stamps the **ruling seat** automatically — that is the record of who
called it, and `--reason` is the ruling itself, mandatory in practice on another seat's

removed the seat boundary, not the requirement to have looked. **Stale default:** one

## The one question

Tier does **not** follow how hard the task looks. It follows:

> ## 🔑 If this goes wrong, WHO CATCHES IT?

Our register of failures is not bad code — it is **plausible answers nobody
disbelieved**: seven instruments returning confident wrong counts in one session;
~40 bridge calls reporting success and changing nothing; an `<li>` discarding a
whole def and costing 26 biomes. Cheap models are safe exactly where failure is
loud, and dangerous exactly where it is silent.

| Who catches a wrong answer | Use |
|---|---|
| It is an **OS-level search** (grep, glob, file inventory) whose result is re-checked | **sonnet** |
| A **compiler, selftest, validator or hook**, before anyone reads it | **sonnet** |
| **Another agent**, who will re-derive it before acting | **sonnet** |
| **Nobody** — it becomes a recorded fact other work cites | **opus** |
| **Only taste** — art, the world, prose he reads | **opus** judge agent (not the maker), then his curated review — `design/RimMandrake/delegation_policy.md`; the naive pre-review of anything shown to him is this row (`standing_rulings.md` §Nothing reaches the owner unread) |

⛔ If you cannot name the catcher, you are on row 3. "It'll be obvious" is not a catcher.

### 🔴 Sonnet vs Opus — owner ruling, 2026-10-29 (replaces "Sonnet default, self-escalate after one failed attempt")

> "Sonnet for building code that can easily be checked right via tests and output. Opus for code
> that is challenging to validate directly, has no valid tests for much of its function, or
> knowledge work where quality is subjective."

The test is whether a test or output can say the work is right, not how hard it feels.

- **Opus:** C#/Harmony behaviour with no selftest; concurrency and restart code (seat restarts,
  leases, locks); orchestration and dispatcher logic (`rimflow`, `dispatcher_schedule`); design;
  art judgment; specs, rosters, taxonomies; triage or verification judgment with nobody to catch it.
- **Sonnet:** XML defs and patches that `validate_patch` checks; fixes a selftest proves; deploys;
  quicktests; greps, censuses and searches.
- **Unsure: Opus.** Put `model: opus` on the spawn. Escalate the model, never the ceremony: the same short leash.

## Helpers in this repo

The method is the `efficient-subagents` skill (and `agent-fanout-research` for a fan); this adds what's true here.

- **Spawn only the `rm-*` definitions** (`.claude/agents/`, enforced by `.claude/hooks/block_unbounded_agent.py`):

  | type | use | model |
  |---|---|---|
  | `rm-fixer` | well-defined fix a selftest/validator proves | sonnet |
  | `rm-builder` | complex code or design, one item | opus |
  | `rm-bridge` | live-game section run by script | opus |
  | `rm-judge` | art/taste judging of work it did not make | opus |

- **Unattended seats: at most 3 helpers per seat** (the allocator's limit). In the Conductor window there is no limit only for work started within
  20 min of the owner's last typed message; after that two helpers, and one running over an hour raises an alarm (owner: "...only for work started within
  20 mins of the last time the user typed to conductor. After that it should relax to two subagents only."). Measure:
  `python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/token_census.py --since <UTC>`.
- **Worktrees are OFF:** never pass `isolation: "worktree"` (`block_worktrees.py` refuses it). A writing helper edits in the window's own clone and the window
  commits its paths with `./publish`. A helper that needs its own clone gets
  `python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/scratch_clone.py clone "<purpose>" --fetch --sparse <the dirs it will touch>`, never `--checkout` (the whole ~4 GB tree).
- **Cutting claims from a doc:** the two-blind-arms method in `efficient-subagents`, with `src/RimMandrake/Utils/doc_claims.py` numbering the claims.
- **Cheap read-only fan-out:** `src/RimMandrake/Utils/nemotron_fanout.py` and `nemotron_ceiling.py`; the measured pool, its ranking and the abstention clause are in
  `research/FANOUT_WORKER_EVALUATION.md`.
- **One live-game lane at a time.** Several helper lanes that each need the running game starve one another (one lane waited 45 minutes and tested nothing): run at most one live-game lane, and batch the live checks. A bridge hold goes stale after 45 idle minutes and another window can then take the bridge, killing a helper's live session: keep the hold fresh with an event inside every 45 minutes during long helper runs.
- **Split art redraws one agent per subject.** An art-regeneration agent works one picture at a time (eight redraws took ~20 min in one agent); launch them in parallel, one agent per subject.
- **Briefs for helpers that edit a previously clean file say: 'mark-clean only after reading every line'.** Helpers tend to re-mark such a file clean after reading only their own hunks. The orchestrator checks each report for 'hunk' or 'diff only' wording and reopens the file with `python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/code_review_status.py reopen`.
- **`infrastructure/state/code_review/<SEAT>.jsonl` is one shared file per seat, and parallel helpers collide on it.** Helper A's mark-clean lines sit uncommitted beside helper B's, and the commit hook forces a pathspec commit, which takes the whole working-tree file, so neither can commit its own marks without sweeping the other's (staging a HEAD-plus-your-lines blob with `update-index` is refused too, because a pathspec-less commit is refused). Commit mark-clean lines in the same Bash turn as the mark, or let the last helper of the wave (or the parent) commit the shard once all are done. Open fix: one shard per helper, or a `code_review_status.py` verb that commits only the caller's tagged records.
- **Grep memory before relaying a fact about factions, biomes or rulings to the owner.** A subagent's unverified fact reached the owner wrong (a DLC's empire named as the wrong faction) when a memory file held the right answer.
- **Debugging is script-first (`design/RimMandrake/debug_process.md`).** A live poke that ends without its lesson committed as a check (plus the informative false theories) is lost work: the `ns_probe_*` scratch files vanished and survived only in commit messages.
- **The Conductor stays conversational.** Never block the owner's window on long foreground waits (sleep/until loops, multi-minute checks) or chain hidden steps; push waits to background and answer him in plain words first. Owner: "Conductor is supposed to be someone I can easily chat with about how it's going... Almost the opposite of the design intention" and "This procedure is opaque. What are you even doing?"
- **Before drafting from an item's text, check it against later rulings.** A brief can carry a mechanism a later owner ruling voided (TWILIGHT_BOTTOM_CAST_1 still named 'lease practice' after "The Compact does NOT sell light... Remove." (owner)). Grep the item's design dir for an existing draft and read the later sibling passes' 'Ruled' headers first.
- **Say what happened and how you know in the first clause of a status line.** 'No longer in the running list' reads as lost or dropped to the owner; v3 had simply finished.
- **More than ~10 concurrent helpers closes the fewest items per token.** Burn days with 10-22 helpers spent 99.5M cache-read tokens per closed item (30 closes), against 5.2M on the framework-guided day at 4-7 concurrent and 11.2M in ALMOST_OUT. Spend surplus tokens on durable no-review work (harnesses, instruments, wiring), not on more parallel helpers or review waves.
- **Delegation did not stop the owner's card load.** After `delegation_policy.md` he still answered 207 card questions in 4.1 days (~50/day vs ~76/day before); 144 were in classes already delegated (design 57, process 58, art picks 29). Agreement with the agent's Recommended option there was only 50-61%, so most were real choices; ordering/helper-count cards (81% agree) and twin-apply cards (86%) are pure leak. On his own sheet marks, agents' 'wait/keep' recommendations matched him 39%, while a 'newest mark wins, x acts now' rule predicts 83%.
- **No subagent type can reach Artifact/ArtifactData** (rm-fixer lacks ToolSearch; rm-builder's ToolSearch finds neither; general-purpose is hook-blocked). A helper gathers the data into a file and the write goes through a headless `claude -p` with `CLAUDE_CODE_ARTIFACT=1` (`src/RimMandrake/Utils/fleet_refresh.py`). Helper types need `SendMessage` in their tools list to report mid-run (added to rm-builder, rm-fixer, rm-bridge): a brief must not tell a running helper to message anyone unless its type has the tool.
- **`code_review_status.py list` (bare) silently omits every never-entered file; use `--show-untracked` for the true DIRTY pool.** A loop run without it reported "0 DIRTY" for 43 waves while 346 files were invisible. Do not compare the raw file count with the CLEAN count: CLEAN entries can exceed the current file count (`[x2]`-style repeat marks on renamed or moved paths); judge the remaining pool by `--show-untracked`'s own reported count.
- **Builders mark their OWN new files CLEAN in `code_review_status`, and a reviewer then found 3 real bugs in files the builder had marked clean.** A self-mark is not a review: briefs must say 'do not mark your own files CLEAN', and independent reviewers re-read author-marked files in full rather than trusting the mark.

## Subagents — this is where the saving is

🔴 **Every `Agent` call takes `model`. Pass it, every time**
(`block_agent_without_model.py` refuses otherwise; it also blocks named agent types such as `Explore` called without an explicit `model`, despite the hook text exempting named types).

| Job | Model |
|---|---|
| OS-level search: grep, glob, inventory, "does X exist", fixed-shape census; extraction/classification with a checkable result | **sonnet** |
| Well-defined coding a compiler, selftest or validator will check | **sonnet** |
| Sweep where the agent must interpret or classify | **sonnet** |
| Fan-out whose returns will contradict; adversarial refutation | **sonnet** |
| **Design** — a spec, a roster, a taxonomy, anything the owner reads as design | **opus**, backgrounded |
| **Complex code generation** — a new system, Harmony/C#, cross-file changes with no test to catch them | **opus** |
| Anything acted on **without re-deriving it** | **opus** — and ask why it is a subagent |

A subagent's return is EVIDENCE, never a finding — it carries CONFIRMED/UNCERTAIN
and the window decides what is true. Never spawn a duplicate for "reliability".
- **A subagent report ending `HANDOFF READY` is the agent's own artifact, not a handoff.** Only the seat's handoff ritual (`handoff.py --check`) licenses that line. Parallel helpers must not share one stage folder: `selftest_winstage` once staged every clone in one shared folder so agents tested each other's source (now a per-clone hash).
- **Never run heavy ML from a subagent inside a seat.** Model downloads, torch, ComfyUI, mesh generators and big numpy rasterizers inherit the seat's cgroup; one 7 GB child pushed the 10 GB scope to its limit with swap full, the kernel killed it, and the window died anyway (`OOMPolicy=continue` only stops systemd tearing the scope down). Run such a job in its own bounded systemd scope so a balloon kills only itself. Local generation is parked; do not relaunch it without the owner's word.
- **A backgrounded `Agent` dies at 600 s of silence and leaves NOTHING on disk** (a clean tree, a whole run lost; survivors had streamed output by 385 to 575 s). Brief every writing subagent to create its output file as a skeleton FIRST and fill it section by section: a file write emits progress and persists partial work. A long read-then-write brief is the shape that trips it. For a **mechanical** census (glob, parse, count, tabulate), writing the script inline costs less than briefing an agent to survive the watchdog; reserve subagents for work that needs judgement.

## Four places a cheaper tier is forbidden outright

1. **Deciding whether an instrument told the truth** (`BUILDABLE.md` exists because they lie).
2. **Live bridge writes** — the world is frozen and hand-authored, no regenerate behind it.
3. **The world, and art** — *"iterate by LOOKING"*; realism is not scoreable.
4. **Text the owner reads as a conclusion** — above all a number.
   ↳ 🔴 **One carve-out, owner ruling 2026-09-16: north-star `must read` verdicts.**
   Verbatim: *"Let a model YES green a line."* A model judging a mod's letter or
   flavour prose against a `must read` line MAY return a pass, and that pass greens
   the line — it is not routed to him. The tier floor still applies (opus), and
   `cannot read` lines stay absolute. Rationale and the residual risk are in
   `design/RimMandrake/north_star_validation_spec.md` §10.4: the rule it replaced
   would have made any text-first mod permanently ungreenable unattended, and an
   off-register letter is a bounded, recoverable failure. **This carve-out is
   read-verdict-only** — a number, a count, or a finding he will act on still lands
   on row 3 and still comes to him.

## Hooks and Claude Code session quirks
- **A `PreToolUse` hook added to `.claude/settings.json` mid-session does not fire** — not for this window's Bash calls and not for its subagents' — until a new session starts; a hook already present at session start does fire for subagents. Test a new hook in a fresh window, never by exercising it in the one that added it.
- **A Claude Code hook marked `asyncRewake` survives its session's kill** (re-parented to /init, would wait its full 23 h timeout; measured on Claude Code 2.1.308). Any long-waiting async hook must find its claude ancestor at start and exit when that pid dies (`doorbell.claude_ancestor` + `owner_pid` guard).
- **A Claude Code transcript (`~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/<session>.jsonl`) logs one line per content block of an API message, each repeating the SAME usage:** sum usage once per `message.id` (last line wins) or a run is overcounted 2-3x; deduped it reproduces the `claude -p` result json exactly. A role run's `--name` is not in the jsonl: find it by session id (pin with `--session-id`) or by the "role launch <unit>" text in the first user line (`role_launch.transcript_usage`).
- **The Claude Code `WorktreeCreate` hook's real stdin is `cwd, name, prompt_id, session_id, transcript_path`** (the docs say `base_path`/`worktree_name`, which is wrong). `WorktreeRemove` never fires (0 of 11 runs). The hook's parent pid is a dying `sh -c`: walk `/proc` up to the `claude` process to find the session.
- **A PreToolUse Bash hook matches its trigger word anywhere in the command text, even inside a heredoc that only mentions it,** and a refusal rejects the whole compound command so its other steps do not run. Two seen: the art-push hook refuses any command containing the repo's push-script word while HEAD carries art events whose PNGs are not committed (for example after a sibling helper swept your art-shard lines into its commit); the registry-write hook refuses a heredoc patch that merely names the modcheck status file. Keep the word out of the command: write prose with Write/Edit, put the patch in a scratch file, and run it.
- **Replaying hook payloads is not read-only:** an allowed `Agent` call makes `block_agent_over_slots.py` reserve a real helper slot for 90 s (`spawn_reservations.json`). Any tool that feeds hooks synthetic Agent calls must set `RM_SPAWN_RESERVE_S=0`, as `hook_latency.py` does.
- **`AskUserQuestion` is validated by `validate-question-card.py`:** a `header` longer than **12 characters**, or a question not ending in `?`, refuses the **whole card**. Count the header before calling. (The `Agent` tool likewise refuses without an explicit `model`; see the ladder above.)
- **`claude -p --json-schema` takes the schema TEXT, not a file path** (`claude -p --help`). With `--output-format json` the validated object is the top-level key `structured_output` (`result` also holds it as a string). A schema using `/pattern/` and `anyOf` is accepted.
- **Headless `claude -p` CAN use ArtifactData (measured):** set `CLAUDE_CODE_ARTIFACT=1` and unset the inherited `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-cli` (CLI gate `sdk_default_off`); keep the Artifact tool enabled (ArtifactData vanishes without it); a parts write by `file_path` is a Read, so allow `Read(//<dir>/**)`; overwriting an existing doc needs `if_version`. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS=1` + `--disable-slash-commands` cut ~8k uncached tokens/run. Working example: `src/RimMandrake/Utils/fleet_refresh.py`.
- **A `claude -p` loop launched with `--setting-sources project` skips the user's effort setting and runs at medium with no warning:** pass `--effort`. A running pass does not take a changed settings file; its next pass does.

## The loop (seat)

```
./publish -m "subject" path/one path/two        # commit those paths, replay onto origin/main, push; prints PUBLISHED <sha>
land.sh <sha> <path>...                         # land one commit already made (any clone; plumbing)
land.sh -m "subject" <path>...                  # land working-tree bytes of the paths without a local commit
./sync                                          # realign this clone's main with origin/main (seat_sync.py)
```

- `./publish` (`src/RimMandrake/Utils/publish.py`) commits by pathspec, re-creates any local commit not yet upstream on
  origin/main by plumbing (`merge-tree` + `commit-tree`), moves main there with `git reset --keep`, pushes, and retries up
  to 8 times when origin moved. It **never stashes**, so it works in a dirty clone: it refuses only on a real conflict or
  when you hold an uncommitted edit to a file origin changed, naming the path, with your commit intact on HEAD.
- `land.sh` (`src/RimMandrake/Utils/land.sh`; `/home/mandrake/.seat-tmp/land.sh` is a one-line wrapper) publishes ONE
  commit or explicit paths by plumbing, retries a lost push race, then runs `./sync --no-fetch` itself. `LAND_REPO`
  defaults to the clone the cwd is in. stdout is exactly `PUBLISHED <sha>`; pass it to `rimflow close --sha`.
- `./sync` moves main to origin/main with `git reset --keep` only when every local commit is already upstream (git cherry
  `-`, or the same bytes per path) and no dirty file holds bytes other than upstream's; else it prints `REFUSED: <why>`
  and changes nothing. Local commits go to `backup/<seat>-pre-sync-<stamp>-<sha>`. Never stash, never `--hard`.
- Pathspec on the commit (`git commit <paths>`), never `git add -A`/`.`/`-a` (hook-enforced). Never `--force`. Never a file over ~50 MB.
- Proof of publication is `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main`, never an empty `git log origin/main..HEAD` and never the exit code: `./publish` can exit 120 with no output yet have pushed.
- Origin is SSH (`git@github.com:Lmandrake/RimMandrake.git`).
- Committed and pushed is the only durable state: commit at each finished unit and push at once.
- Do not `git pull --rebase` in a seat clone: it refuses on ANY dirty file, and a seat clone is always a little dirty.

## Traps

Each of these cost at least one lost or mis-published change. Most are hook-enforced or fixed in the tools above; the
rest are discipline.

| trap | what happens | do instead |
|---|---|---|
| `git add a b c 2>/dev/null` | one missing path fails the WHOLE add silently; the commit then runs on an empty or partial index and "succeeds" | never silence `git add`; check `git show --stat HEAD` |
| a deleted path on `git add` | `git add <deleted>` errors and kills the `&&` chain; the push after it says "Everything up-to-date" | put a deleted path on the commit pathspec only |
| pathspec commit takes the WORKTREE | `git commit <path>` is an implicit `git add` of that path: a blob you staged with `update-index` is ignored, and a peer's unsaved lines in the same file ride along | check `git diff --stat <path>` first; build partial commits in a temp index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`) |
| pathspec commit cannot remove-but-keep | `git rm --cached p` then `git commit p` re-adds `p` from the worktree | commit through a temp index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=… git read-tree HEAD; git rm --cached …; write-tree; commit-tree`), then `git reset -q -- p` in the real index |
| untracked can't be pathspec-committed | `git commit <new file>` → "did not match any file(s) known to git"; a `git commit <dir>` silently skips new files in it | `git add -- <new file>` first (explicit path), then `git commit <paths>` |
| `-F -` after `--` | `git commit -- p -F -` treats `-F` and `-` as pathspecs | options before `--`, paths after |
| bare `git commit` | commits the WHOLE index, including what a helper staged in the same clone | always name paths (hook-enforced) |
| `.git/index.lock` exists | a background helper's read-only `git status` holds it for a second; a failed `./publish` then committed NONE of its paths | wait a few seconds and retry; never delete a lock younger than a minute; check `git status` after any failed publish |
| compound command refused whole | a `PreToolUse` hook (blanket stage, DLL stamp, sheet guard) refuses the entire Bash call before the shell runs — any file write chained before the commit never happened either | keep file writes and git commands in SEPARATE Bash calls; a hook's refusal means nothing in that call ran |
| zsh refspec modifier | `git push origin $N:refs/heads/main` — zsh reads `:r` as a modifier and mangles the refspec | `"${N}:refs/heads/main"` |
| land.sh duplicates | landing by plumbing leaves the clone "ahead N, behind M" with patch-equivalent copies; a stale clone shows phantom selftest reds (ledger_lint NOT_APPEND, a "lost" bridge tool) | `land.sh` now syncs itself; otherwise `./sync`. Re-check a red on a synced clone before fixing it |
| autostash | `pull --rebase --autostash` re-applied peers' dirty files and stranded 53 in `stash@{0}` (2026-10-10) | never stash; `./publish` and `./sync` use `reset --keep` |
| pre-push ledger lint judges the LOCAL HEAD | a correct plumbing push from a clone behind origin is refused NOT_APPEND | `./sync` first, then land |
| served review-sheet output | all of `Transient/` is untracked since 2026-10-18 except `*.decisions.json` and pins; `refresh_sheets.py` prints `UNPUBLISHED:` only for a rebuilt sheet that is pinned (tracked) | publish a pinned rebuilt sheet; an unpinned one needs nothing |
| a fetch OOM-kills the window | fetching the 5.5 GiB pack inside a 10G-capped seat scope | `systemd-run --user --scope --quiet -p MemoryMax=20G git fetch origin main` |
| a real merge commit | the blanket-stage hook refuses `git commit --no-edit` mid-merge (no pathspec possible) | `GIT_EDITOR=true git merge --continue` |
| `handoff.py` UNPUSHED gate refuses a fully published tree | the gate compares SHAs, not patches; publish rebases, so the local SHAs differ from origin's | prove equivalence with `git log --cherry-mark origin/main...HEAD`, then `./sync`; do not reach for `--force` |
| `handoff.py --wake` in a stale shared checkout | it prints that checkout's newest handoff, not origin's, so a window can wake on an old one | read `git show origin/main:infrastructure/state/handoffs/<newest>` instead |
| a plumbing-built push (patch diffed from the wrong parent, `git apply` failing inside a pipe to `tail`) | pushed an EMPTY commit with a misleading message | assert the apply succeeded (`set -o pipefail`) and that the resulting tree differs from `origin/main` before pushing |
| `git commit && git pull --rebase && git push` in ONE Bash call | the pre-push/PreToolUse ledger hook judges HEAD BEFORE the compound runs, so it is refused NOT_APPEND even though the rebase would fix it | run commit, pull/rebase and push as separate Bash calls; never stash a peer's dirty files to rebase (`./publish` replays without a stash) |
| `./publish` refuses ('not mine to overwrite', `reset --keep` refused, exit 2) because a PEER has an uncommitted edit to a file origin changed, or to the mod DLL pair (their `winbuild.py` output, `+dirty` in the `.srchash`) | your commit stays local and every later publish waits on that peer; the temp-index + `commit-tree` + push workaround is refused by the ledger_lint push hook, which lints the stale local HEAD | land WITHOUT touching the tree: `tree=$(git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=C^ origin/main C)`; `commit-tree` it onto `origin/main`; `git push origin <tip>:main` (local main stays diverged; the next publish's `git cherry` skips it). Or from a throwaway `git clone --shared --no-checkout <seat clone> /home/mandrake/rm/scratch/<SEAT>/land`: set `origin` to the real remote, `checkout -B main origin/main`, cherry-pick, push (there HEAD IS origin+1, so the lint passes). Ledger shard lines: append only the new ones. For a peer's dirty DLL pair only: back the pair up under `D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\backups\`, `git show HEAD:<path> > <path>` for both files, `./publish` (it rebuilds from committed source), then `winbuild.py <Mod>` again so the working copy carries the peer's source. Tell the report whose edit blocked it |
| `./publish` replay stops on YOUR commit, or refuses a DLL conflict because a helper's commit in the same clone was replayed (local HEAD keeps its pre-replay twin), in a clone dirty with peers' files | rebase, `--autostash` and stash are all refused or destructive there | rebuild the local chain by plumbing (`git merge-tree --merge-base=c^` + `commit-tree`, your conflicted file given as a resolved blob via a temp `GIT_INDEX_FILE`), re-check HEAD has not moved, then `git reset --keep` to the new tip.
